Vulnerabilities.Title: ca-certificates - security update
Vulnerabilities.Description: Description Not Available

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc-toolset-15-gcc: gcc: gcc-toolset-16: gcc: Denial of Service via use-after-free in binary heap erase_if
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC. When an application calls the erase_if function on a binary heap priority queue in libstdc++, the library reallocates storage but fails to update its internal entry pointer. An attacker capable of triggering this operation can exploit this use-after-free condition, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an application crash or potential memory corruption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Confirmed out-of-bounds read/write in libstdc++ parallel `std
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC. An out-of-bounds memory access vulnerability exists in the libstdc++ parallel search implementation due to an undersized internal buffer. A local attacker can exploit this flaw by providing crafted search data to an application compiled with parallel mode, causing the process to crash and leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Integer wrap in `std
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in the libstdc++ component of GCC. An attacker who can provide an excessively large element count to a boolean vector (std::vector<bool>) constructor can trigger an integer wrap during internal memory calculations. This issue leaves the container in an inconsistent state, leading to out-of-bounds memory access and resulting in an application crash or a Denial of Service (DoS) during subsequent operations.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Stack overflow in std::bitset on libstdc++
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC libstdc++. When an application extracts data into a bitset from a wide-character stream, internal stack memory allocation fails to properly account for character size and alignment. An attacker capable of supplying crafted input to an affected application could trigger a stack-based buffer overflow leading denial of service (DoS).

Vulnerabilities.Title: libstdc++: overflow leaves streambuf in inconsistent state on I/O error.
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in libstdc++. When a byte-by-byte write operation fails during file stream processing, the library may still append data into the internal memory buffer. An attacker capable of inducing repeated write failures in an affected service can trigger a buffer overflow, potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: libstdc++ integer overflow in `new` operator
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in libstdc++. An integer overflow can occur when processing large inputs to the aligned operator new in the C++ library. This vulnerability could lead to an undersized memory allocation, potentially causing memory corruption or application instability.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Out-of-bounds read in std::from_chars
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in gcc. An attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by passing a string that is not null-terminated to the std::from_chars() function in the libstdc++ library. This issue triggers an out-of-bounds read beyond the allocated buffer, potentially leading to invalid data parsing or an application crash.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: glibc: Memory corruption via out-of-bounds write in wide scanf functions
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Calling the wide scanf family of functions (swscanf, fwscanf, wscanf, vswscanf, vfwscanf and vwscanf) with a %s or %[ conversion without the 'l' length modifier in the GNU C Library version 2.2 to version 2.44 writes an extra null byte one past the end of the destination array when the converted multibyte string and its terminating null byte exactly fill that array.

These conversions store each wide input character into the caller's char array as a multibyte sequence.  The conversion ends with the sequence that returns to the initial shift state, which also stores the terminating null byte, and the functions then append a second null byte.  A destination sized for the converted string and one terminator, as the C standard requires the caller to provide, is therefore written one byte past its end.  The out-of-bounds byte is always a null byte, which may corrupt adjacent data or crash the process.  An attacker who supplies the input can trigger the overflow with a string whose converted length exactly fills the destination.

The narrow scanf functions, the %ls and %l[ conversions into a wchar_t array, and the 'a' and 'm' allocation modifiers are not affected, and storing a wide scanf conversion into a narrow char array is uncommon.  This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: glibc: Heap buffer overflow via attacker-controlled fopen mode string
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Passing an effectively empty string to the `,ccs=` syntax extension of the mode argument in the `fopen` function in the GNU C Library version 2.45 or earlier may result in a heap buffer overflow when the mode string input to the function is attacker controlled.



This usage pattern is not seen in applications in common GNU/Linux distributions and applications that process user-supplied values for `ccs` should not pass them through without validation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: Buffer Overflow in strfmon right-justification padding
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Calling strfmon and strfmon_l in the GNU C Library version 2.38 to 2.44 can write past the end of the caller-supplied output buffer when a conversion uses right-justified width padding.

Exploitation requires an application code path that calls strfmon or strfmon_l with right-justified width padding into a destination buffer that is large enough for the padding to succeed but too small for the internal memmove call. The field width or format may be attacker-influenced or a fixed susceptible pattern in the caller.

At the time of publication, no network-facing application impact is known.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: Fix out-of-bounds array write in tdelete
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Calling tdelete on a sufficiently deep tree in the GNU C Library version 2.1 to 2.44 may write one pointer past the end of an alloca-allocated array on the stack, which may crash the application.

The tdelete implementation keeps an explicit stack of parent nodes for rebalancing, which is grown as needed while descending the tree.  Two rebalancing branches push an additional entry without checking the capacity, and write past the array when the stack is exactly full. Triggering this requires a node at a depth of exactly 40 (or 40 plus a multiple of 20), which implies a tree with at least a million nodes, so an attacker must drive a large number of insertions and deletions through an application that uses tsearch and tdelete.  The written value is a pointer into a tree node and is not directly attacker controlled.  No affected application in common distributions has been identified.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: glibc: Out-of-bounds write via TSIG record processing
Vulnerabilities.Description: The deprecated functions ns_printrrf, ns_printrr and fp_nquery in the GNU C Library version 2.2 and newer fail to enforce the caller-supplied buffer length, and can result in an out-of-bounds write when printing TSIG records.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: glibc: Application crash or uninitialized memory read via crafted DNS response
Vulnerabilities.Description:
The deprecated functions ns_printrrf, ns_printrr and fp_nquery in the GNU C Library version 2.0.1 to version 2.43 fail to validate the RDATA content against the RDATA length in a DNS response when processing A6, CERT, LOC, TKEY or TSIG records, which may allow an attacker to craft a DNS response, causing a target application to crash or read uninitialized memory.

These functions are for application debugging only and hence not in the path of code executed by the DNS resolver.  Further, they have been deprecated since version 2.34 and should not be used by any new applications.  Applications should consider porting away from these interfaces since they may be removed in future versions.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: glibc: Process abort due to invalid memory in wordexp
Vulnerabilities.Description: Calling wordexp with WRDE_APPEND in the GNU C Library version 2.0 to version 2.43 can cause the interface to return invalid memory in the we_wordv member, which on subsequent calls to wordfree may abort the process.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: Glibc: Denial of Service via stack exhaustion during tilde expansion
Vulnerabilities.Description: When expanding paths that begin with a tilde (~) followed by a username, the internal parse_tilde function extracts the username to determine the user's home directory.  The implementation allocates memory for this username directly on the stack using the strndupa macro. Because the size of this allocation was determined by the length of the user-supplied input without any bounds checks, passing an excessively long username e.g. thousands of characters, forces the thread to exhaust its stack space. Thus if an application passes untrusted, attacker-controlled input to the wordexp function, an attacker can trigger a stack clash.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: Non-progress DoS in SHIFT_JISX0213 -&gt
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Converting crafted SHIFT_JISX0213 input to UCS-4 or the internal wide character encoding, for example with iconv, in the GNU C Library version 2.3 to 2.44 may result in the converter making no progress, causing the calling application to hang.

Some SHIFT_JISX0213 sequences decode to two code points.  If the output buffer has room for only the first one, the converter stores the second in the conversion state and returns E2BIG, but it never clears that pending character after emitting it on the next call.  The converter then keeps emitting the pending character without consuming further input, so an application that retries the conversion loops forever. The input must be attacker controlled and the application must convert it with an output buffer small enough to split the two code points. Only the SHIFT_JISX0213 character set is affected, which is not commonly used.  The related defect in the EUC_JISX0213 converter is tracked separately as CVE-2026-80489.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: Non-progress DoS in EUC_JISX0213 -> UCS-4 conversion state
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Converting crafted EUC_JISX0213 input to UCS-4 or the internal wide character encoding, for example with iconv, in the GNU C Library version 2.3 to 2.44 may result in the converter making no progress, causing the calling application to hang.

Some EUC_JISX0213 sequences decode to two code points.  If the output buffer has room for only the first one, the converter stores the second in the conversion state and returns E2BIG, but it never clears that pending character after emitting it on the next call.  The converter then keeps emitting the pending character without consuming further input, so an application that retries the conversion loops forever. The input must be attacker controlled and the application must convert it with an output buffer small enough to split the two code points. Only the EUC_JISX0213 character set is affected, which is not commonly used.  The related defect in SHIFT_JISX0213 converter is tracked separately as CVE-2026-77117.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: glibc: Arbitrary code execution via directory traversal in LANGUAGE environment variable
Vulnerabilities.Description:
The gettext family of functions in the GNU C Library version 2.0 and later accept LANGUAGE environment variable entries that contain '/' or that are equal to "..", unless the program is setuid or setgid (AT_SECURE).  An attacker who can set LANGUAGE in the environment of a program that uses gettext can make it load a message catalog (.mo file) from an arbitrary location in the file system.  A crafted .mo file can crash the program through out-of-range offsets, or supply translations whose format directives do not match the arguments passed by the program.  That causes undefined behaviour in the printf family of functions and may allow arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the program.  The safety of message catalogs relies on them being installed in trusted, read-only locations, and the directory traversal bypasses this.

The fix for CVE-2014-0475 rejects ".." path components in locale names passed to setlocale or taken from the LC_ALL, LC_* and LANG environment variables.  gettext reads LANGUAGE directly and appends each colon-separated entry to the message catalog directory, so that fix did not cover LANGUAGE.

LANGUAGE is only used when the LC_MESSAGES locale is not "C", "C.<encoding>" or "POSIX", so the attacker must also be able to select another installed locale, for example through LANG or LC_ALL.  Exploitation also requires that the attacker can place the crafted file in a location readable by the target program, and that the environment crosses a trust boundary without the program running as AT_SECURE.  An example is an SSH server that accepts LANGUAGE and LANG from clients through the AcceptEnv directive and restricts an account to a forced command; the attacker may use this to escape the restriction.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: glibc DNS stub resolver: Denial of Service via long search domain in configuration
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Initializing the DNS stub resolver from an /etc/resolv.conf file, or a LOCALDOMAIN environment variable, whose search list contains a domain of roughly 200 characters or more in the GNU C Library version 2.26 to 2.44 results in an assertion failure which aborts the process.

The resolver truncates the search list when copying it into the fixed-size _res.defdname buffer, then asserts that the copy is consistent with the full configuration.  The consistency check compared against the wrong size and did not handle a first entry that does not fit, so a correctly truncated list failed the assertion.  Any process that resolves names through the library is affected, including long-running processes that reload /etc/resolv.conf on the next query after it changes.  Search domains are commonly written to /etc/resolv.conf from data received over DHCP or from a VPN server, so an attacker on the local network may be able to trigger this without privileges on the target system, subject to validation by the network configuration software.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: glibc: Privilege escalation and arbitrary code execution via TOCTOU race condition in dynamic loader
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in the dynamic loader (ld.so) of the GNU C Library (glibc) versions 2.14 through 2.44 allows a local attacker to escalate privileges. When expanding $ORIGIN in DT_RPATH for setuid/setgid (AT_SECURE) programs, glibc validates the lexically normalized search path against the trusted directories but then opens the raw, un-normalized path. On systems where the Linux fs.protected_hardlinks sysctl is disabled, a local attacker who hard-links such a program into an attacker-controlled directory and wins a race to replace an intermediate path component with a symbolic link can direct the loader outside the trusted directory, causing it to load an attacker-controlled shared object and execute arbitrary code with the elevated privileges of the program.

Exploitation requires an installed setuid or setgid binary whose DT_RPATH uses $ORIGIN followed by ".." traversal that normalizes into a trusted directory, and the ability to hard-link that binary and win the race by swapping a path component for a symbolic link. Major Linux-based OS distributions ship with fs.protected_hardlinks enabled by default and mitigate the vulnerability.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: nscd stack overflow leads to degraded DNS resolution
Vulnerabilities.Description:
The nscd service in the GNU C Library 2.3.4 onwards may crash due to a 
stack overflow when a malicious DNS server returns too large a response 
for a DNS query, resulting in degraded DNS resolution for the system.



Exploitation of this bug needs a system that has nscd enabled and using 
an untrusted DNS server for name resolution, with the compromised DNS 
server being capable of processing records large enough to result in a 
stack overflow in an nscd thread stack.  During experimentation, bind 9 
was unable to handle large records, but that could change in future or 
with a different name server.  In typical installations, nscd is 
executed in an isolated context as its own user without a shell, due to 
which any compromise of that service is isolated.



There is a remote possibility of nscd cache corruption if an attacker 
manages to get the stack pointer into a desired point in the heap, 
potentially resulting in other caches in nscd being overwritten with 
corrupt data through the stack overflow, until the buggy code path 
eventually results in a crash.



Finally, a crash in nscd may result in performance degradation when 
resolving names, but it does not result in a denial of service.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: glibc: Local attacker can cause denial of service and information disclosure via stack-based buffer overflow.
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A stack-based buffer overflow in the dynamic loader (ld.so) of the GNU C Library (glibc) versions 2.14 through 2.44 allows a local attacker to crash or corrupt the memory of setuid/setgid (AT_SECURE) programs.

When such a program's DT_RPATH or DT_RUNPATH begins with $ORIGIN and is followed by NUL or '/' the loader both reads past the end of the path buffer and writes past the end of a stack-allocated internal buffer. The corrupted loader stack can lead to a loader crash (denial of service) and limited disclosure of process memory.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: glob implementation can cause excessive CPU and memory consumption due to crafted glob expressions
Vulnerabilities.Description: The glob implementation in the GNU C Library (aka glibc or libc6) allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service (CPU and memory consumption) via crafted glob expressions that do not match any pathnames, as demonstrated by glob expressions in STAT commands to an FTP daemon, a different vulnerability than CVE-2010-2632.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: uncontrolled recursion in function check_dst_limits_calc_pos_1 in posix/regexec.c
Vulnerabilities.Description: In the GNU C Library (aka glibc or libc6) through 2.29, check_dst_limits_calc_pos_1 in posix/regexec.c has Uncontrolled Recursion, as demonstrated by '(\227|)(\\1\\1|t1|\\\2537)+' in grep.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: stack guard protection bypass
Vulnerabilities.Description: GNU Libc current is affected by: Mitigation bypass. The impact is: Attacker may bypass stack guard protection. The component is: nptl. The attack vector is: Exploit stack buffer overflow vulnerability and use this bypass vulnerability to bypass stack guard. NOTE: Upstream comments indicate "this is being treated as a non-security bug and no real threat.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: running ldd on malicious ELF leads to code execution because of wrong size computation
Vulnerabilities.Description: GNU Libc current is affected by: Re-mapping current loaded library with malicious ELF file. The impact is: In worst case attacker may evaluate privileges. The component is: libld. The attack vector is: Attacker sends 2 ELF files to victim and asks to run ldd on it. ldd execute code. NOTE: Upstream comments indicate "this is being treated as a non-security bug and no real threat.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: ASLR bypass using cache of thread stack and heap
Vulnerabilities.Description: GNU Libc current is affected by: Mitigation bypass. The impact is: Attacker may bypass ASLR using cache of thread stack and heap. The component is: glibc. NOTE: Upstream comments indicate "this is being treated as a non-security bug and no real threat.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: information disclosure of heap addresses of pthread_created thread
Vulnerabilities.Description: GNU Libc current is affected by: Mitigation bypass. The impact is: Attacker may guess the heap addresses of pthread_created thread. The component is: glibc. NOTE: the vendor's position is "ASLR bypass itself is not a vulnerability.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: uncontrolled recursion in function check_dst_limits_calc_pos_1 in posix/regexec.c
Vulnerabilities.Description: In the GNU C Library (aka glibc or libc6) through 2.29, check_dst_limits_calc_pos_1 in posix/regexec.c has Uncontrolled Recursion, as demonstrated by '(|)(\\1\\1)*' in grep, a different issue than CVE-2018-20796. NOTE: the software maintainer disputes that this is a vulnerability because the behavior occurs only with a crafted pattern

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: glibc: Denial of Service via memory allocation failure during regular expression processing
Vulnerabilities.Description:
The regcomp and regexec functions in the GNU C Library version 2.3 to version 2.44 may read freed memory and free the same heap block twice when a memory allocation fails while a regular expression is compiled or matched.  The re_dfa_add_node (the NFA node table) and build_range_exp (bracket ranges) grow several arrays with consecutive realloc calls and store the new pointers only after all of them succeed.  When a later call fails, the pattern buffer keeps pointers to blocks that were already freed, and the error cleanup frees them again.  In regexec, the back-reference cache (match_ctx_add_entry) frees its array when a realloc fails but keeps the pointer, which is freed again on the error path.

An attacker does not need to supply a crafted regular expression: patterns large enough to grow these arrays are common.  The failure has to hit a specific allocation, though, so the issue can only be reached when the system is already under memory pressure.  An attacker who supplies the pattern or the subject string has little control over which allocation fails, so the expected impact is a crash of the process.  This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: glibc: Denial of Service via double free in glob functions
Vulnerabilities.Description:
The glob functions in the GNU C Library versions 2.44 and earlier may free the same heap block twice when a memory allocation fails while glob prepends the directory name to the names it matched.  The names already rewritten are freed, but their pointers stay in the result vector, and the error path frees them again with globfree.

The allocation must fail after at least one name has been rewritten, so the issue can only be reached when the process is already close to its memory limit, for example under an address space limit (RLIMIT_AS) or on a 32-bit system.  The attacker needs control to make the result large enough to make the program or service run out of memory, either by controlling the glob pattern and having knowledge of the filesystem layout or through other means.  This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.

Vulnerabilities.Title: glibc: glibc: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in strncasecmp
Vulnerabilities.Description:
The strncasecmp function in the GNU C Library 2.24 and later optimized for the Power8 architecture may read one byte beyond the input size limit, which may crash a program when that byte is not readable.

This condition may happen when the input strings to the strncasecmp function are attacker controlled in an application and they match all the way up to the edge of their page and the neighbouring page is either not mapped or is not readable.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Converting crafted CP949 input to UTF-8 character encoding and ignorin ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Converting crafted CP949 input to UTF-8 character encoding and ignoring invalid characters, in the GNU C Library version 2.1 or later may result in the converter reading past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling application to crash.

When the CP949 decoder encounters an invalid input byte sequence like '\xa2\xe8' it ends up advancing the pointer tracking the read buffer position twice.  If //IGNORE is set on the destination encoding and this sequence is at the end of the input buffer, the decoder may then end up reading past the bounds of the input buffer.  To exploit this, the target iconv function needs to set //IGNORE on the destination of the conversion and the input and encoding needs to be attacker controlled.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Converting crafted ISO-2022-CN-EXT input to UTF-8 character encoding,  ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Converting crafted ISO-2022-CN-EXT input to UTF-8 character encoding, in the GNU C Library version 2.2 through 2.44 may result in the converter reading past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling application to crash.

When the ISO-2022-CN-EXT decoder encounters an invalid input byte sequence like '\x0e' it ends up advancing the pointer tracking the read buffer position twice.  If this sequence is at the end of the input buffer, the decoder may then end up reading past the bounds of the input buffer.  To exploit this, the input and encoding needs to be attacker controlled.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Converting crafted input from UCS-4 to IBM1390 or IBM1399 character en ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Converting crafted input from UCS-4 to IBM1390 or IBM1399 character encoding, in the GNU C Library version 2.3.3 and later may result in the converter reading past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling application to crash.

When converting from UCS-4, these encoders may encounter a combining base such as U+00E6 and jump ahead by 4 bytes to check the next UCS-4 code point.  The check for end of buffer however does not account for this, which may result in a buffer overread if the following code point has less than 4 bytes remaining.  Exploitation of this bug not only requires attacker control of input and encoding, but also strict control over layout of the input in memory.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via memory leak in QUIC stream handling
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: A QUIC server that rejects a stream opened by the peer may
retain that stream's state for the lifetime of the connection if the peer
resets the stream before the rejection is signalled, even though the peer's
stream credit is returned.

Impact summary: A remote client that completes a QUIC handshake can repeatedly
open and reset streams, causing server memory to grow without bound until the
process runs out of memory and every connection on it is lost. This is a
Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

Description: QUIC servers track each stream the peer opens. When the incoming
stream policy rejects a stream, OpenSSL schedules a STOP_SENDING frame, marks
the stream deleted and returns the peer's stream credit. A deleted stream is
collected only once its receive part is fully drained, which for a rejected
stream means the STOP_SENDING has been acknowledged. If the peer sends
RESET_STREAM first, the reset cancels the pending STOP_SENDING, so it is never
sent or acknowledged and the stream is never collected.

The default configuration reaches this path. Once a connection has a default
stream, meaning the application has read from or written to the connection as
the tutorial server does, the effective incoming stream policy rejects streams
the application does not accept. Applications that set the REJECT policy
explicitly are affected too.

Each retained stream costs about 300 bytes, and the peer's stream credit
window paces how quickly they accumulate. A client that keeps the connection
open and keeps opening and resetting streams grows server memory without
bound. The severity is Low because growth is slow, needs a long-lived
connection, and causes no memory corruption or disclosure.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via crafted EC certificate in CMS encryption
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: Encrypting a CMS message to an EC certificate whose group order
is 1 may cause CMS_encrypt() or CMS_encrypt_ex() to loop indefinitely.

Impact summary: An attacker able to supply the recipient certificate to an
application performing CMS encryption can cause that application to loop
indefinitely, consuming CPU and resulting in Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-835: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')

Description: CMS_encrypt() and CMS_encrypt_ex() encrypt a message to one or
more recipient certificates and, for an EC recipient, generate an ephemeral
key in the recipient's group. If the certificate declares a group order of 1,
random scalar generation can only produce zero. The key generation routine
then retries without limit while waiting for a nonzero private scalar, so the
call never returns.

The OpenSSL TLS and QUIC implementations do not use this path. An application
is exposed only if it calls CMS_encrypt() or CMS_encrypt_ex() with a recipient
certificate whose EC parameters are attacker-controlled. Certificates with
normal EC group orders do not trigger the loop.

OpenSSL 4.0 and later reject unknown explicit EC groups in default builds.
These versions are affected only when configured with the
enable-ec_explicit_curves option.

The result is a hang that consumes a CPU core until the process is
interrupted, a Denial of Service. The severity is Low because the attacker
must supply the recipient certificate and the application must choose to
encrypt to it; ordinary CMS encryption to trusted recipients is unaffected.

The fix makes EC key generation fail when the group has no valid nonzero
private scalar, instead of retrying indefinitely.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules in 4.1, 4.0, 3.5 and 3.0 are not affected. The FIPS provider
does not support arbitrary explicit EC domain parameters, so an order-1 group
is rejected during key import before the vulnerable key generation path is
reached.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via crafted CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData message
Vulnerabilities.Description: Verifying a maliciously crafted CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData message with CRL checking enabled may consume excessive CPU time, growing with the square of the message size.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read during TLS key-share processing
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: A server configured with the Suite B certificate flag through
SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags() and with TLS 1.3 enabled may read past the end of a
fixed group list when it processes a ClientHello whose supported_groups and
key_share contain no Suite B group.

Impact summary: A remote client can send a ClientHello that makes the server
read past the end of a static array. The values read are never returned to the
client, so no memory is disclosed; on builds with sanitizers or hardened
allocators the read may crash the process, causing Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read

Description: When the Suite B certificate flag is set, OpenSSL restricts the
accepted groups to P-256 and P-384 by substituting a fixed two-element list
for the configured group list. The tuple machinery used for key-share
selection was not updated for this substitution: tls1_get_group_tuples() still
returns the configured tuples, which by default describe eight groups. The
server-side walk in tls_parse_ctos_key_share() then advances through the
two-element list using those tuple counts without checking the cumulative
offset against the number of groups present.

Only applications that call SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags() with
SSL_CERT_FLAG_SUITEB_128_LOS and leave TLS 1.3 enabled are affected. The
openssl s_server -suiteB_128 option sets an X.509 verification parameter
instead, so the stock command line server is not vulnerable. Default
configurations do not reach this code.

A client that offers only groups outside the Suite B set, such as X25519,
forces every tuple to be walked and the read to run past the array. The bytes
read are compared against client group IDs and never sent back, so no memory
is disclosed. On builds with address sanitizers or hardened allocators the
read can abort the process; in ordinary release builds it reads a few bytes of
adjacent constant data.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: OpenSSL: Denial of Service via NULL pointer dereference during DANE TLSA record processing
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: A DANE-enabled TLS client may crash by dereferencing a NULL
pointer when processing an unusual combination of certificate and TLSA
records.

Impact summary: The impact is limited to a client crash (potential Denial
of Service).

CWE: CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference

Description: A DANE-enabled TLS client that supports TLSA records with at
least one of the PKIX-TA(0) or PKIX-EE(1) usages alongside the DANE-TA(2)
usage may crash by dereferencing a NULL pointer if the server claims a trusted
CA's certificate to be its end-entity certificate and has an unusual mix of
associated TLSA records.

DANE SMTP clients should not be affected since only the
DANE-TA(2) and DANE-EE(3) TLSA record usages are specified applicable
in SMTP.  For example, the Postfix MTA is not affected, while the Exim
MTA does not at present use OpenSSL's DANE implementation.

Use of DANE in validation of RFC7250 raw public keys (RPKs) is also
unaffected, as these only use DANE-EE(3) TLSA records.

Only applications that support combining the DANE PKI with a traditional PKI
are potentially affected.  A DANE-enabled browser or similar, that uses
OpenSSL's DANE API could be affected.

FIPS impact: no
The DANE API is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Denial of service via crafted out-of-sequence DTLS handshake fragments
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: Receiving crafted out-of-sequence DTLS handshake fragments may
cause OpenSSL to allocate a full message-length reassembly buffer for each
buffered message, so a small amount of wire data consumes a large amount of
memory.

Impact summary: A remote attacker can send a few small crafted DTLS handshake
fragments to make a DTLS server or client allocate well over a megabyte of
memory per connection, which may lead to memory exhaustion and Denial of
Service if many connections are made.

CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

Description: DTLS handshake messages can arrive out of order and fragmented,
so OpenSSL buffers fragments of up to ten out-of-sequence messages until
reassembly is possible. When the first fragment of a new message arrives,
OpenSSL allocates a buffer sized to the full message length declared in the
fragment header, plus a reassembly bitmap, instead of storing only the bytes
actually received. The declared length is capped by the maximum certificate
list size, 128KB by default, and that cap applies to every handshake message
type rather than only to Certificate messages.

Only DTLS endpoints reach this code. TLS, QUIC and applications that do not
use DTLS are unaffected. An attacker sends fragments that declare a large
message length but carry almost no data, using up to ten distinct message
sequence numbers.

A single connection can then hold roughly 1.4MB of buffers from about 156
bytes on the wire. Because the number of buffered messages is capped, memory
exhaustion requires many connections or many peers, which is why the severity
is Low.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via overlapping QUIC CRYPTO frame processing
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: A retransmitted QUIC CRYPTO frame can release packet storage
while the TLS record layer retains a direct pointer into that storage causing
use after free.

Impact summary: A malicious QUIC server can cause a heap-use-after-free read
in the OpenSSL QUIC client. The server can also identify one allocator-adjacent
byte through the client's protected Handshake response.

CWE: CWE-416: Use After Free

Description: During CRYPTO stream processing, a pointer into the first frame's
memory on the stream is lent to the TLS handshake processing. The memory
must remain stable until it is processed and released. However the processing
of retransmitted CRYPTO frames could release the memory if the retransmitted
frame fully overlapped the existing frame. This then causes use-after-free read
when the TLS handshake processing continues.

The use-after-free read can lead to a Denial-of-Service of the client
application or a minor leak of information about the heap memory contents
that might be overwritten with other data, subsequently allocated by
the application, to the peer.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS module is not affected as the QUIC implementation is outside of
the OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: OpenSSL: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in AES-GCM-SIV
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: Setting an AES-GCM-SIV IV shorter than the expected nonce
length via EVP_CipherInit_ex() may trigger a heap out-of-bounds read.
Supplying a longer IV is silently truncated instead of rejected.

Impact summary: An application passing a caller-supplied IV of the wrong
length may crash or read beyond its buffer. Because trailing IV bytes are
ignored, an attacker who knows one message and tag may forge messages under a
different IV.

CWE: CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read

Description: AES-GCM-SIV copies the caller-supplied IV or nonce into its
internal state using a copy whose length is taken from the expected nonce size
rather than from the length the caller actually provided. When the caller
passes a shorter IV, the copy reads past the end of the caller's buffer;
AddressSanitizer confirms a heap out-of-bounds read reached through
EVP_CipherInit_ex() into ossl_aes_gcm_siv_init(). When the caller passes a
longer IV, the implementation silently discards the trailing bytes instead of
rejecting the length.

The truncation breaks the binding between the IV and the computed
authentication tag. An attacker who has observed a message and its tag under
one IV can produce a message and tag that verify under a different IV whose
first bytes match, since the surplus bytes never influence the computation.
The message itself is unchanged, so this is a failure of IV commitment rather
than a classic existential forgery.

Only applications that call EVP_CipherInit_ex() (or the equivalent provider
cipher initialization) with an IV length other than the standard 12 bytes for
AES-GCM-SIV are affected. The severity is limited because the out-of-bounds
read is small and attacker-controlled only in length, and the forgery requires
an unusual IV length choice by the application.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules are not affected by this issue, as AES-GCM-SIV is not an
approved algorithm.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via malformed PEM data in PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: When an application passes a stack to
PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() to add entries to, and reading fails,
OpenSSL frees every entry in the stack, both the old ones and any new
ones, but leaves them in the stack.

Impact summary: An application that passes an existing stack to
PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() and keeps using it after a failed read may
use memory that was already freed. This can cause a crash or, in
principle, memory corruption. Malformed PEM data can make the read fail,
but only applications that pass an existing stack are affected, and
OpenSSL itself does not do this.

CWE: CWE-416: Use After Free

Description: PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() reads certificates, CRLs and
private keys from PEM data and adds them to a stack of X509_INFO
structures. If the application passes a stack that is not NULL, the
function adds the new entries to it and must leave the entries that are
already there unchanged.

If reading fails, the function frees every entry in the stack. This
includes the entries that were there before the call, and the entries
added by the call. It does not remove these entries from the stack, so
the stack keeps pointers to freed memory. The failure can happen at any
point, even before any entry was added. A PEM item with invalid content
is enough.  This also happens if the stack was empty: entries added
before the failure are freed but stay in the stack.

An application that then reads or frees the stack will use memory that
was already freed. This can crash the application or, in principle,
corrupt memory.

Only applications that pass a stack that is not NULL are affected.
OpenSSL itself never does this. Its own callers, including the code that
TLS uses to load CA certificates, always pass NULL. When the stack is
NULL, the function frees only the entries that it created itself, which
is safe. We expect that very few applications pass an existing stack. An
attacker can make the read fail with malformed PEM data, but cannot make
an application pass an existing stack.

The same problem affects PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio(), PEM_X509_INFO_read()
and PEM_X509_INFO_read_ex(), which use the same code. OpenSSL 1.1.1 and
1.0.2 have only the first two of these functions.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Out-of-bounds write via integer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock()
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: Calling EVP_EncodeBlock() with an input length close to INT_MAX
may overflow the calculation of the encoded output size and write past the end
of the caller-supplied output buffer.

Impact summary: No path by which an attacker can trigger this has been
identified. An application that passes an input length near INT_MAX to
EVP_EncodeBlock() could suffer a heap buffer overflow, crashing or corrupting
its own memory, but it must itself supply such a length.

CWE: CWE-190: Integer Overflow or Wraparound

Description: EVP_EncodeBlock() base64-encodes a buffer of a caller-supplied
length into an output buffer that the caller allocates. The caller is expected
to reserve 4*((len+2)/3)+1 bytes. For input lengths close to INT_MAX, the
arithmetic that computes the encoded length overflows a signed integer, so the
function writes more data than the documented output size. The result is a
heap buffer overflow in the calling process.

Reaching this requires an application to pass an input length near INT_MAX to
EVP_EncodeBlock(). OpenSSL's TLS, QUIC and CMS implementations never encode
buffers of that size, and the command line tools cannot practically be made to
do so: the limits on reading a proxy password from a file and on bignum sizes
prevent it. An application that accepts an attacker-controlled length and
forwards it to EVP_EncodeBlock() without its own bound check is exposed.

The severity is Low because no attacker-controlled path to the overflow is
known. The caller must already hold a buffer of about two gigabytes before the
defect can be reached.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: openssl: Information disclosure via uninitialized memory in QUIC peer detection
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: QUIC, when performing automated peer detection, may allow
uninitialized stack data to leak into the received address which is then used
as the destination for outgoing packets.

Impact summary: Applications using QUIC's automated peer detection mechanism
may receive an invalid address, leading to connection loss and disclosure of
uninitialized stack data to an attacker observing the outgoing network traffic.

CWE: CWE-457 (Use of Uninitialized Variable)

Description: The OpenSSL QUIC stack contains a feature in which, when using an
already connected socket, it will auto-detect the peer address during the SSL
handshake.  This feature uses the getpeername() function, passing a buffer of
sufficient length to hold any supported address family, but passes a buffer
length that is only sized such that larger addresses, such as IPv6, cannot be
retrieved. The getpeername() function however, still returns the full address
length, which is accepted as the valid input buffer length, leading to the
address buffer containing uninitialized stack data instead of the actual peer
address. The invalid peer address is then used as destination for the outgoing
packets which leads to a connectivity breakage and a leakage of the
uninitialized stack data to passive network observers.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules in 4.0, 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, and 3.0 are not affected by this CVE as
the affected protocol is not implemented in the FIPS module.

Vulnerabilities.Title: openssl: OpenSSL: Message authentication bypass via zero-length AAD update
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Issue summary: The AES-GCM-SIV implementation treats a zero-length Additional
Authenticated Data (AAD) update as a reset of all the AAD supplied so far,
instead of leaving the AAD unchanged. An application that supplies its AAD in
several fragments, one of which is empty, therefore produces or verifies
messages whose authentication tag does not cover the AAD supplied before
the empty fragment.

Impact summary: Data an application intended to authenticate alongside a
message is silently left unauthenticated. An attacker can forge the AAD of such
a message.

CWE: CWE-325: Missing Cryptographic Step

Description: An application passing AAD in multiple chunks of which some have
zero length will have the previous AAD chunks effectively unauthenticated. Also,
on context re-initialisation, the AAD was not reset, which meant that any AAD
accumulated from the previous context usage were also included in the AAD of the
new message.

The fix makes a zero-length AAD update a no-op and clears any accumulated AAD
whenever the context is re-initialised with a key or a nonce.
A re-initialisation that only changes parameters keeps the AAD.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS modules are not affected, as AES-GCM-SIV is not a FIPS approved
algorithm and is implemented only in the default provider, outside the
OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc-toolset-15-gcc: gcc: gcc-toolset-16: gcc: Denial of Service via use-after-free in binary heap erase_if
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC. When an application calls the erase_if function on a binary heap priority queue in libstdc++, the library reallocates storage but fails to update its internal entry pointer. An attacker capable of triggering this operation can exploit this use-after-free condition, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an application crash or potential memory corruption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Confirmed out-of-bounds read/write in libstdc++ parallel `std
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC. An out-of-bounds memory access vulnerability exists in the libstdc++ parallel search implementation due to an undersized internal buffer. A local attacker can exploit this flaw by providing crafted search data to an application compiled with parallel mode, causing the process to crash and leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Integer wrap in `std
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in the libstdc++ component of GCC. An attacker who can provide an excessively large element count to a boolean vector (std::vector<bool>) constructor can trigger an integer wrap during internal memory calculations. This issue leaves the container in an inconsistent state, leading to out-of-bounds memory access and resulting in an application crash or a Denial of Service (DoS) during subsequent operations.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Stack overflow in std::bitset on libstdc++
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC libstdc++. When an application extracts data into a bitset from a wide-character stream, internal stack memory allocation fails to properly account for character size and alignment. An attacker capable of supplying crafted input to an affected application could trigger a stack-based buffer overflow leading denial of service (DoS).

Vulnerabilities.Title: libstdc++: overflow leaves streambuf in inconsistent state on I/O error.
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in libstdc++. When a byte-by-byte write operation fails during file stream processing, the library may still append data into the internal memory buffer. An attacker capable of inducing repeated write failures in an affected service can trigger a buffer overflow, potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: libstdc++ integer overflow in `new` operator
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in libstdc++. An integer overflow can occur when processing large inputs to the aligned operator new in the C++ library. This vulnerability could lead to an undersized memory allocation, potentially causing memory corruption or application instability.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Out-of-bounds read in std::from_chars
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in gcc. An attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by passing a string that is not null-terminated to the std::from_chars() function in the libstdc++ library. This issue triggers an out-of-bounds read beyond the allocated buffer, potentially leading to invalid data parsing or an application crash.

Vulnerabilities.Title: zlib: zlib: Heap buffer overflow in gz_vacate() allows arbitrary code execution
Vulnerabilities.Description: zlib 1.2.11 through 1.3.2 contains a heap buffer overflow: after an underlying write() fails, gz_write() returns without resetting strm.next_in, leaving it pointed at the caller's buffer. A later gz* write call then derives a position from the stale pointer and writes past a heap allocation; any write() failure reaches it, including EPIPE on a blocking descriptor, and in versions before 1.3.1.2 the failed write must be followed by a gzclearerr() call.

Vulnerabilities.Title: zlib: zlib: Denial of Service via infinite loop in CRC32 combine functions
Vulnerabilities.Description: zlib before 1.3.2 allows CPU consumption via crc32_combine64 and crc32_combine_gen64 because x2nmodp can do right shifts within a loop that has no termination condition.
